{
  "segment_function": "prologue introducing the significance of the 1957 satellite launch as an expression of the human desire to escape earth imprisonment and the human condition through science and technology",
  "claims": [
    {
      "claim": "The immediate reaction to the 1957 satellite launch was relief about the first step toward escaping human imprisonment to the earth rather than unmitigated triumph.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "The immediate reaction, expressed on the spur of the moment, was relief about the first “step toward escape from men’s imprisonment to the earth.”",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "qualifications": [],
      "confidence": 1.0
    },
    {
      "claim": "The question of whether to use scientific and technical knowledge to exchange given human existence for a self-made existence is a political question of the first order.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "The question is only whether we wish to use our new scientific and technical knowledge in this direction, and this question cannot be decided by scientific means; it is a political question of the first order and therefore can hardly be left to the decision of professional scientists or professional politicians.",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "qualifications": [
        "cannot be decided by scientific means"
      ],
      "confidence": 1.0
    }
  ],
  "definitions": [],
  "distinctions": [],

  "responses": [],
  "references_to_other_sections": [],
  "unresolved_context": [
    "Implications of the potential repudiation of the Earth as the Mother of living creatures and the rebellion against human existence as given."
  ],
  "must_not_be_lost": [
    "The 1957 satellite launch represents a turning point in human desires regarding earthly imprisonment and the human condition."
  ]
}
